title: Unpacked-extension service worker keeps running stale code after rebuild — verify the running bundle before trusting measurements
trigger: E2E/browser measurements don't change after rebuilding dist, or instrumentation markers never appear in the SW global scope
principle: Quetta (and Chromium forks) can keep an unpacked extension's service worker on the previously registered script across browser restarts and even across `registration.update()` — the loader file is re-served from cache. Content scripts DO load fresh per page, so UI-side changes appear to work while every SW-side change is silently dead. Hours of profiling can measure old code. Reliable invalidation: bump `manifest.version` in the source manifest (dist differs → extension update → SW reinstall). Verify the running code with a module-load marker (e.g. `globalThis.__orchLoaded = Date.now()` at module top) read back via `serviceWorker.evaluate()` — if the marker is absent after a lookup, the SW is stale. Note `--load-extension` pointing at a different directory with the same extension ID is ignored when the profile already has that ID registered.

cases.context: Dictionary lookup optimization on real Quetta: phraseIndexCache + ArrayBuffer blob changes built into dist, loader pointed at the new hashed bundle, yet all LOOKUP_REQUEST timings stayed ~1.3-1.8s and __lt/__orchLoaded markers stayed undefined — the SW was executing the pre-change bundle the whole time.
cases.bad: Rebuild dist → relaunch browser with --load-extension=dist → measure → conclude the optimization didn't help.
cases.good: Bump manifest version (or relaunch until the SW re-registers) → confirm a load-marker global exists in sw.evaluate() → THEN measure. world cold 679ms / warm 10ms on the new code vs ~1.3s phantom 'warm' on the old code.

applyFor: Any real-browser verification of SW-side changes on an unpacked MV3 extension
When UI metrics improve but message-level/SW metrics don't move after a rebuild
Before claiming a performance regression or fix — always prove which code the SW ran
